item.title: 49ers are becoming the thirty-something Niners, adding to Super Bowl urgency
item.description: Fred Warner (54), DeForest Buckner (99) and Osa Odighizuwa (92) in the first half Sunday as the San Francisco 49ers played the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi's Stadium. (Carlos Avila Gonzalez/S.F. Chronicle) The San Francisco 49ers entered this season with one the NFL's oldest rosters. Then general manager John Lynch swung two midseason trades - for 32-year-old defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and 34-year-old wide receiver Keenan Allen - that boosted his team's average age even further. Lynch's actions have prompted a legitimate question for many 49ers fans: Do he and head coach Kyle Shanahan have an affinity for older players? And if so, why? "I don't think that's, like, a conscious thing," Lynch said Thursday morning on KNBR. "We're not saying, ‘Let's go find every old guy.'" The 49ers' roster sits at an average age of 28.0, according to Pro Football Reference, which is the highest number in the league. They have 18 players who are 30 or older, and that number will rise to 19 in a week when linebacker Fred Warner celebrates his 30th birthday. "Hell yeah!" tight end George Kittle said Thursday, upon being alerted to this stat in the locker room. But history does not favor the 49ers in this regard. The last team to win a Super Bowl with an average age of 28? The 2003 New England Patriots, who had a whopping 24 players age 30 or older. No team has won a ring with even 18 players this old since the 2009 New Orleans Saints. What makes this 49ers team especially unique, though, is that the large majority of their veterans have never won a Super Bowl. Wide receivers Mike Evans and Demarcus Robinson are the lone players in San Francisco's 30-and-older crew to have reached the mountain top (Robinson did it twice). This roster is full of players who have put in time - a lot of time - but have never reaped the ultimate reward. Players like Buckner, Allen, tackle Trent Williams , center Jake Brendel and 40-year-old long snapper Jon Weeks have spent at least a decade in the NFL and never won a ring. For San Francisco's core group of players who made Super Bowls in 2019 and 2023 yet painfully saw both opportunities slip away, the sting hurts a little more. Think Kittle, Deebo Samuel , Dre Greenlaw , Fred Warner, Kyle Juszczyk , Nick Bosa . The 49ers own a 7-1 record and look like a formidable NFC contender. This might be their last best chance to win a ring. The pressure is heightened. How do all these factors affect the psyche of a locker room? "When you have a veteran team - especially a veteran team with a lot of guys who have played really good football and unfortunately haven't gotten to that part of it - I think it's a big driving factor for a lot of us. item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. item.description: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night. “I’m not anticipating him being back this season,” Lanning said. “Really got clarity for us this past week, for him,” Lanning added. “And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night Let’s catch you up. What does the starting lineup look like? The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. What about the rotation? Micah Nori , the Blazers’ first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams’ availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it’s likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well. Wait … the Blazers have a new coach? The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter . Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. The Blazers’ coaching position had been embroiled in controversy, of course, as former coach Chauncey Billups — who was placed on indefinite leave by the NBA — is facing federal felony charges related to money laundering and wire fraud conspiracy for his alleged involvement in a rigged underground poker game. What style will the Blazers play? In a stark contrast to recent seasons, the Blazers are constructed around their offense rather than their defense. item.title: Top MLB Agent Reveals Red Sox Have Goal of Beating Yankees Entering Offseason
item.description: Top MLB Agent Reveals Red Sox Have Goal of Beating Yankees Entering Offseason originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There's a lot of hope within the Boston Red Sox organization that the team is going to be among the best in baseball next season. The Red Sox already showed throughout the 2026 campaign that at any given moment, they can be a team that has a chance to win a World Series. Unfortunately for the Red Sox, they didn't play well in a three-game set against the New York Yankees, losing the first two games of the Wild Card Series. The Red Sox are going to have to figure out how they can get past the Yankees and some other teams next year, but there's a ton of talent on both sides of the baseball for them to do just that. There's also an entire offseason for the Red Sox to get better, and according to the latest from super agent Scott Boras, it sounds like their goal is to improve this year. The Red Sox, according to Boras, want to get to a point where they can beat the Yankees, and there's already been some heavy communication indicating that they're willing to do a lot this winter. “They had goals of getting into the playoffs but also have a barrier they want to jump over, and that’s beating the Yankees,” Boras said, per The Athletic . “I think that’s very clear and they want to make their team better and add to it… “I’ll let them decide (on what’s) aggressive,” he said. “All I know, the communication has been heavy, and there’s a real understanding from ownership on down that they want to advance.” The strange part of this year's Major League Baseball offseason is the fact that the Red Sox and other teams around the league are expecting a lockout. Once that lockout happens at the beginning of December, if it does, it's going to throw a wrench into signing free agents. That doesn't mean the Red Sox won't be able to improve before or after then, but this isn't going to be a typical offseason. Regardless, it's very promising to hear that Boston has already been very much in the mix to land some of the top players available, as there are a couple of Boras clients who make a ton of sense to sign for the Red Sox. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.title: Dodgers’ Shohei Ohtani admits frustration despite being in MVP race again
item.description: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Dodgers’ Shohei Ohtani admits frustration despite being in MVP race again appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As expected, Chicago Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong has been named the NL MVP. Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani was a distant second in the voting as his incredible run of three straight MVP awards (one in the AL, two in the NL) finally came to an end. But despite being an MVP finalist for the sixth straight season, Ohtani was far from pleased at how his 2026 season played out . “Honestly, I thought it was a very frustrating season. Obviously, we did not do that well in the playoffs. Personally, I was a little bit frustrated with my overall performance throughout the season. In a nutshell, it wasn’t a great season, personally for me,” Ohtani said via a translator in an interview on MLB Network on Thursday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Ohtani finished the year hitting .275 with 30 home runs and 81 RBIs. He also had arguably his best season as a starting pitcher in MLB, going 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA in 14 starts. However, Ohtani’s performance fell off a cliff late in the season, in part due to injury. In September, he hit just .200 with no home runs and one RBI in 30 at-bats. That poor run carried over in the postseason, where he hit just .194 withe one homer and three RBIs. With Ohtani far from his best, the Dodgers were unceremoniously swept by the eventual World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS to end their three-peat bid. The good news is that Ohtani will not need offseason surgery despite his injury concerns. He and the Dodgers will now be hoping that he can fully recover from his injuries and get back to his MVP-caliber play next season. item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 12: Morgan Rogers of England celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between England and Croatia at Wembley Stadium on November 12, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Michael Regan - The FA/The FA via Getty Images) | The FA via Getty Images England played Croatia yesterday for what seems like the umpteenth time in the last few months, and just like on the previous occasions, the Three Lions triumphed, though this time only by a narrow, 2-1 scoreline. Still, a win’s a win, and Morgan Rogers still managed to find himself among the goals, scoring his third international goal and his second in the last three games. In fact, our record-signing has five goal contributions (2g+3a) in his last eight England appearances, dating back to the knockout rounds of the World Cup. His place in the selection is certainly under no threat. Morgan Rogers goal vs Croatia 🦾 pic.twitter.com/xgvOmDhqqr — Out Of Context Chelsea (@NoContextChe1) November 12, 2026 Unfortunately, the same cannot be said for his bestest friend, Cole Palmer, who was once again left at home by Thomas Tuchel, and once again amid insinuations that our starboy is not committed enough to the England cause. And that’s not just a media narrative, it’s something perpetuated by Tuchel himself. But that’s a bunch of nonsense as far as Rogers is concerned. A flat out “lie”, even. “[That’s] a lie. He wants to be here. He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. People just see it as news and say the easy thing. “We all know he had a difficult year last year with injuries and I know personally he’s been managing them injuries ever since. He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn’t feel 100% himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself. Of course he does, who wouldn’t? But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10 to 15 years, he also has to manage himself. “If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it. It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It’s a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England. You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don’t get it and he doesn’t get it. But it’s something he has to deal with but I can assure you he wants to be here and he wants to play for his country.” -Morgan Rogers; source: The Guardian Spoken like a true friend, and a true professional. Meanwhile, Tuchel is apparently “totally fine” with all of this … or at least will be until results start going against him.

item.title: Shohei Ohtani’s MVP Bid Falls Short After Injury-Marred Dodgers Season
item.description: Not surprisingly, Chicago Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, after an electric season that ended strongly, won the National League MVP award over Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani. The NL MVP voting Crow-Armstrong was consistently stellar for the Cubs, providing elite defense, quality hitting, and plenty of stolen bases. He totaled 45 home runs and 84 extra-base hits, and 41 steals on his way to capturing the much-deserved MVP trophy. Oct 11, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Shohei Ohtani (17) reacts during the eighth inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game one of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images Ohtani finished second, with 26 out of 30 second-place votes, two third-place votes, and two fourth-place votes. This was Ohtani’s sixth straight year in the top three of MVP voting, capping what he has managed to achieve, even if he has fallen short of the award a few times. How Shohei Ohtani lost the MVP In the end, Ohtani fell well short of Pete Crow-Armstrong in cumulative statistics and was only somewhat on par in advanced stats. Ohtani hit .275/.377/.512, with 30 home runs, and a 139 wRC+. PCA, on the other hand, had a .280/.372/.570 with a 157 wRC+. In the first half of the season, Ohtani looked on track for MVP, still on pace for 40+ home runs while posting a 1.79 ERA with 95 strikeouts and just 26 walks. However, he stopped pitching in early July; his swing was compromised for the rest of the season, and he missed a handful of weeks. Oct 7, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Shohei Ohtani (17) celebrates after scoring a run against the Atlanta Braves during the second inning in game four of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Bicep, left knee, and even neck inflammation all flared up at different points, and he looked to be noticeably wincing throughout the year. It is impossible to know if he could have avoided his MVP loss with a preventative approach injury-wise, hitting the IL earlier in the year, and possibly getting the issues out of the way earlier so they don’t linger. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) Knowing how competitive Ohtani is, while he’ll surely give the nod to PCA this year, he’ll go hard next year to reclaim his throne.

item.title: Cowboys Add Kendre Miller To Practice Squad After Releasing Reddy Steward
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys added running back Kendre Miller to their practice squad on Wednesday. This move came after the team released defensive back Reddy Steward to clear a spot. Miller joined the squad one day before the trade deadline, and no other major changes were made. The team now has a fresh option at running back while waiting to see how the current group performs in the next ten games. Miller brings a strong track record from his time at TCU before joining the NFL. According to reports, he rushed for 2,410 yards and 26 touchdowns during his three-year college career. He also caught 29 passes for 229 yards and one more touchdown while at the university. With 1,399 rushing yards, he topped the Horned Frogs during a notably strong 2022 season. That performance placed his career rushing total 14th in program history. A Coach Who Prefers Internal Options The Cowboys did not make a single trade before the deadline on Tuesday, outside of October 1st when they traded for Joey Porter Jr. at Cornerback. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer addressed the lack of moves directly when reporters asked him about it. “I’m very comfortable in our team,” he said on Monday regarding the potential for a trade, according to Blogging The Boys . The decision to keep the roster stable comes at a time when backup Tyler Goodson is dealing with a knee sprain. Goodson had a career game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday before the injury occurred. The team needed depth quickly, which led them to bring in Miller. He reunites with running backs coach Derrick Foster, who also coached him when Miller was with the New Orleans Saints in 2024. This existing relationship should help him learn the system faster. Clearing the Roster for New Blood Steward had played in three games for Dallas this season, starting two of them. He was elevated from the practice squad specifically for the games against Baltimore, Houston, and Tampa Bay. During those three outings, he tallied 11 total tackles. Steward initially joined the team in August of 2025 and played in all 17 games last season. Miller was cut by the New Orleans Saints on Saturday in his fourth season since being drafted. In the third round of the 2023 draft, the Saints selected him. His 7.5 yards per carry average as a sophomore in 2021 led the entire nation. His recent NFL time was limited. The next test for this group is a big one this coming Sunday, Nov. 15, when the San Francisco 49ers visit AT&T Stadium. The game kicks off at 4:25 p.m. ET. The Cowboys are currently 4-5 and trail the 5-2-1 New York Giants in the division standings.

item.title: Opponent Defensive Preview: Michigan State Spartans
item.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 07: Savion Hiter #5 of the Michigan Wolverines is tackled by Cam Stodghill #12 of the Michigan State Spartans during a first half run at Michigan Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week, the Huskies will travel to East Lansing to face off against the 3-6 Michigan State Spartans. The Dawgs are coming off a home loss to Penn State after a valiant comeback attempt, and will look to right the ship against what should be a fairly motivated Michigan State team, especially on the defensive side of the ball, as they held a flailing Michigan team to just 6 points. Defensive Overview Joe Rossi coordinates the defense, which may surprise some, as Rossi was retained when Jonathan Smith was fired and Pat Fitzgerald brought in. According to “O” Basse of The Only Colors, they operate mainly out of nickel due to the injuries that have plagued that side of the ball. Rossi’s Spartan defense currently ranks 62nd in the nation, giving up 337 yards per game (5.4 yards per play). That’s fairly middle of the road, but it’s a fair bit better than 2025, when they ranked 104th. In their 3 wins, they gave up 273, 219 and 192 yards respectively (to Toledo, Eastern Michigan, and Michigan, in that order). Now, it may be because of the talent difference or awful scheming (in Michigan’s case), but this solid defensive showing in victories was predicted by SB Nation’s Michigan’s State site The Only Colors, where they had this to say: While I don’t expect MSU to suddenly be among the conference’s best, I don’t think getting to a more middling rank (7th-12th) should be out of the question. Some parts of the defense should be better than others, naturally, but each group has its guys who will be supplying us with some highlights. They are currently 14th in the Big Ten, and as last week showed, they do have some talent. Safety Devin Vaught (who leads the Spartans with 53 tackles and 2 interceptions) had a pick against Michigan last week. Corner Nikai Martinez had 7 tackles to take his season total to 25, and also has 3 pass deflections and a forced fumble. At linebacker, Cam Stodghill (16 tackles), Brady Pretzlaff and Caleb Wheatland (each with 14 tackles) each are players to watch, with the absence of Jordan Hall. But the big story of last week, according to The Only Colors, was EDGE Anelu Lafaele : Earlier in the season, he appeared to be more of a situational pass rusher, someone the Spartans could unleash off the edge in obvious passing situations. item.title: Bruins Routed by Canadiens on ‘Homecoming’ Night
item.description: BOSTON – The Boston Bruins dropped their first home game since October 5 in a 5-2 loss to the Montreal Canadiens (12-3-4) on Homecoming night at TD Garden. Casey Mittelstadt (7) scored twice, but that was all the Bruins had in store on Thursday night. Jeremy Swayman made 13 saves on 17 shots in 28:14, and Michael DiPietro made 12 stops in relief. The Canadiens got off to a quick start. Kirby Dach opened the scoring just 2:34 into the game. He got the puck from Arber Xhekaj , wrapped around Swayman’s net, and beat him from the left side . Josh Anderson doubled the Canadiens’ lead just six minutes later. Jake Evans redirected a shot from Mike Matheson , and Anderson got behind Mason Lohrei and buried the rebound five-hole on Swayman. The Bruins started the second period strong. They pinned the Canadiens in their own zone and caught them in a long change. However, as soon as the Canadiens got the puck out of their zone, Jake Evans was off on a breakaway and beat Swayman to make it 3-0 . Cole Caufield worked the puck off David Pastrnak ’s stick and raced down the ice all alone. Caufield beat Swayman high with a wrist shot to make it a four-goal game , which ended the night for Jeremy Swayman. Michael DiPietro entered the game after Swayman allowed four goals on 15 shots. The goaltending switch did not change much for the Bruins. Phillip Danault connected on a one-timer from Zachary Bolduc , and he extended the Canadiens’ lead to five . The Bruins snapped Jacob Fowler ’s shutout bid late in the second. Elias Lindholm played the puck to Casey Mittelstadt in the slot, and for his sixth goal of the season, Mittelstadt pulled it to his backhand and beat Fowler. Mittsy gets the B's on the board ✔️ pic.twitter.com/xpNOb8Uxe8 — NESN (@NESN) November 13, 2026 Casey Mittelstadt struck again to start the third period. Play was stopped, and Kreider immediately went down the tunnel . He did not return to Thursday’s game.
